title: Chinese Doggy Bag Culture
synopsis: In a Chinese restaurant, you can almost always ask for a doggy bag (打包). In today’s lesson we learn how this Chinese custom came about and how it can lead to culture clashes.

fullText.simplified:
中国人的打包文化

     “打包”应该算是中国人一个比较特别的习惯。在饭店吃饭，如果还剩有许多菜，中国人一般会选择打包带走，不愿意浪费食物。这个在许多别的国家的人看来，是件非常奇怪的事。就拿日本来说吧，在日本剩饭剩菜是很不礼貌的，所以首先很少会有剩饭剩菜这样的情况。其次，即使有，日本的很多餐馆也是不提供打包的，因为他们觉得打包的食物就不新鲜了。那么，为什么中国人喜欢打包呢？这和中国人的面子文化有一定的关系。
    中国人喜欢请客吃饭，点的菜一般不是一人一份的，而是很多菜，每样菜都是一大盘，大家一起吃。如果点的菜都被吃完了，请客的人会认为是自己点的菜不够，会被别人笑话自己小气，这样会很没有面子。所以请客的人一般会点很多菜，直到客人实在吃不下，剩下来为止。有剩菜，才说明请客的人不小气，是真心诚意地请你吃东西。可是，问题来了，剩下那么多菜，丢了十分浪费，怎么办呢？打包文化就孕育而生了。一般来说，到最后，请客的人会先把客人送出饭店门口，在这期间，店员就把剩下的菜打包起来，等客人走后，再把打包好的菜递给请客的人带走。这样既不浪费食物，也不让请客的人丢面子。
    由于这样的文化差异，有许多日本人到中国来就非常不习惯。他们以不剩下食物为礼貌，中国人以剩下食物为待客之道。结果，你就会看到，日本人拼命地想把桌上的东西吃完，而中国人一看到桌上没有菜了，又继续点菜的现象。
fullText.traditional:
中國人的打包文化

     “打包”應該算是中國人一個比較特別的習慣。在飯店吃飯，如果還剩有許多菜，中國人一般會選擇打包帶走，不願意浪費食物。這個在許多別的國家的人看來，是件非常奇怪的事。就拿日本來說吧，在日本剩飯剩菜是很不禮貌的，所以首先很少會有剩飯剩菜這樣的情況。其次，即使有，日本的很多餐館也是不提供打包的，因為他們覺得打包的食物就不新鮮了。那麼，為什麼中國人喜歡打包呢？這和中國人的面子文化有一定的關係。
    中國人喜歡請客吃飯，點的菜一般不是一人一份的，而是很多菜，每樣菜都是一大盤，大家一起吃。如果點的菜都被吃完了，請客的人會認為是自己點的菜不夠，會被別人笑話自己小氣，這樣會很沒有面子。所以請客的人一般會點很多菜，直到客人實在吃不下，剩下來為止。有剩菜，才說明請客的人不小氣，是真心誠意地請你吃東西。可是，問題來了，剩下那麼多菜，丟了十分浪費，怎麼辦呢？打包文化就孕育而生了。一般來說，到最後，請客的人會先把客人送出飯店門口，在這期間，店員就把剩下的菜打包起來，等客人走後，再把打包好的菜遞給請客的人帶走。這樣既不浪費食物，也不讓請客的人丟面子。
    由於這樣的文化差異，有許多日本人到中國來就非常不習慣。他們以不剩下食物為禮貌，中國人以剩下食物為待客之道。結果，你就會看到，日本人拼命地想把桌上的東西吃完，而中國人一看到桌上沒有菜了，又繼續點菜的現象。

sentences.english: On top of that, even if there are, a lot of restaurants in Japan do not offer doggy bags, ..

sentences.simplified: 那么，为什么中国人喜欢打包呢？
sentences.traditional: 那麼，為什麼中國人喜歡打包呢？

sentences.pinyin: zhè hé zhōng guó rén de miàn zi wén huà yǒu yí dìng de guān xi
sentences.english: So why do Chinese people like to get a doggy bag?
This definitely has a connection with the Chinese culture of saving face.

sentences.simplified: 中国人喜欢请客吃饭，点的菜一般不是一人一份的，
sentences.traditional: 中國人喜歡請客吃飯，點的菜一般不是一人一份的，

sentences.simplified: 而是很多菜，每样菜都是一大盘，大家一起吃。
sentences.traditional: 而是很多菜，每樣菜都是一大盤，大家一起吃。
sentences.pinyin: ér shì hěn duō cài měi yàng cài dōu shì yí dà pán dà jiā yì qǐ chī
sentences.english: Chinese people like to treat others to eat, and the food ordered is usually not one portion per person, ..

sentences.simplified: 如果点的菜都被吃完了，请客的人会认为是自己点的菜不够，会被别人笑话自己小气，这样会很没有面子。

sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ diǎn de cài dōu bèi chī wán le qǐng kè de rén huì rèn wéi shì zì jǐ diǎn de cài bú gòu huì bèi bié ren xiào huà zì jǐ xiǎo qì zhè yàng huì hěn méi yǒu miàn zi
sentences.english: .. but instead they order a lot of dishes, and each dish is brought on a large plate which everyone shares.

sentences.simplified: 所以请客的人一般会点很多菜，直到客人实在吃不下，剩下来为止。
sentences.traditional: 所以請客的人一般會點很多菜，直到客人實在吃不下，剩下來為止。
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ qǐng kè de rén yì bān huì diǎn hěn duō cài zhí dào kè rén shí zài chī bú xià shèng xià lai wéi zhǐ
sentences.english: If you finish all the dishes, the host may feel that they didn’t order enough and will be ridiculed for being cheap and therefore lose face.

sentences.simplified: 有剩菜，才说明请客的人不小气，是真心诚意地请你吃东西。
sentences.traditional: 有剩菜，才說明請客的人不小氣，是真心誠意地請你吃東西。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu shèng cài cái shuō míng qǐng kè de rén bù xiǎo qi shì zhēn xīn chéng yì de qǐng nǐ chī dōng xi
sentences.english: Therefore, the host usually orders a lot of dishes, until the guests are truly unable to finish them all and food is left over.

sentences.simplified: 可是，问题来了，剩下那么多菜，丢了十分浪费，怎么办呢？
sentences.traditional: 可是，問題來了，剩下那麼多菜，丟了十分浪費，怎麼辦呢？
sentences.pinyin: kě shì wèn tí lái le shèng xià nà me duō cài diū le shí fēn làng fèi zěn me bàn ne
sentences.english: If there are leftovers, it shows that the host is not stingy, and has wholeheartedly treated you to a meal.

sentences.simplified: 打包文化就孕育而生了。
sentences.traditional: 打包文化就孕育而生了。
sentences.pinyin: dǎ bāo wén huà jiù yùn yù ér shēng le
sentences.english: Here comes the problem however: leaving that many leftovers would be a tremendous waste, so how do we solve this?

sentences.simplified: 一般来说，到最后，请客的人会先把客人送出饭店门口，
sentences.traditional: 一般來說，到最後，請客的人會先把客人送出飯店門口，
sentences.pinyin: yì bān lái shuō dào zuì hòu qǐng kè de rén huì xiān bǎ kè rén sòng chū fàn diàn mén kǒu
sentences.english: This is how the doggy bag culture was born.

sentences.simplified: 在这期间，店员就把剩下的菜打包起来，
sentences.traditional: 在這期間，店員就把剩下的菜打包起來，
sentences.pinyin: zài zhè qī jiān diàn yuán jiù bǎ shèng xià de cài dǎ bāo qǐ lái
sentences.english: Usually, at the end of the meal, the host escorts the guests to the restaurant’s exit.

sentences.simplified: 等客人走后，再把打包好的菜递给请客的人带走。
sentences.traditional: 等客人走後，再把打包好的菜遞給請客的人帶走。
sentences.pinyin: děng kè rén zǒu hòu zài bǎ dǎ bāo hǎo de cài dì gěi qǐng kè de rén dài zǒu

sentences.simplified: 这样既不浪费食物，也不让请客的人丢面子。
sentences.traditional: 這樣既不浪費食物，也不讓請客的人丟面子。
sentences.pinyin: zhè yàng jì bú làng fèi shí wù yě bú ràng qǐng kè de rén diū miàn zi
sentences.english: .. and after waiting for the guests to leave, the staff hand it over to the host.
This way, not only is food not wasted, but the host also does not lose face.

sentences.simplified: 由于这样的文化差异，有许多日本人到中国来就非常不习惯。
sentences.traditional: 由於這樣的文化差異，有許多日本人到中國來就非常不習慣。
sentences.pinyin: yóu yú zhè yàng de wén huà chā yì yǒu xǔ duō rì běn rén dào zhōng guó lái jiù fēi cháng bù xí guàn

sentences.simplified: 他们以不剩下食物为礼貌，中国人以剩下食物为待客之道。
sentences.traditional: 他們以不剩下食物為禮貌，中國人以剩下食物為待客之道。
sentences.pinyin: tā men yǐ bú shèng xià shí wù wéi lǐ mào zhōng guó rén yǐ shèng xià shí wù wéi dài kè zhī dào
sentences.english: Because of these cultural differences, many Japanese people who come to China have trouble adapting.

sentences.simplified: 结果，你就会看到，日本人拼命地想把桌上的东西吃完，
sentences.traditional: 結果，你就會看到，日本人拼命地想把桌上的東西吃完，
sentences.pinyin: jié guǒ nǐ jiù huì kàn dào rì běn rén pīn mìng de xiǎng bǎ zhuō shang de dōng xi chī wán
sentences.english: For them, not leaving leftovers is considered polite, while Chinese people consider leaving leftovers a way of showing hospitality.

sentences.simplified: 而中国人一看到桌上没有菜了，又继续点菜的现象。
sentences.traditional: 而中國人一看到桌上沒有菜了，又繼續點菜的現象。
sentences.pinyin: ér zhōng guó rén yí kàn dào zhuō shang méi yǒu cài le yòu jì xù diǎn cài de xiàn xiàng
sentences.english: As a result, you may come upon the phenomenon where a Japanese person does their utmost to finish all the food on the table, ..

sentence_translations: Chinese Doggy Bag Culture
The "doggy bag" can surely be considered a quite peculiar custom of the Chinese people.
When having a meal at a restaurant, if there is still a lot of food left over, ..
.. Chinese people will often choose to bring it home in a doggy bag, in order not to waste food.
For people in many other countries, this is seen as a very strange custom.
Take Japan for example: in Japan, leaving unfinished food is considered impolite, ..
.. so they are not very likely to have leftovers to begin with.
On top of that, even if there are, a lot of restaurants in Japan do not offer doggy bags, ..
... because they feel that the food brought home is not fresh.
So why do Chinese people like to get a doggy bag?
This definitely has a connection with the Chinese culture of saving face.
Chinese people like to treat others to eat, and the food ordered is usually not one portion per person, ..
.. but instead they order a lot of dishes, and each dish is brought on a large plate which everyone shares.
If you finish all the dishes, the host may feel that they didn’t order enough and will be ridiculed for being cheap and therefore lose face.
Therefore, the host usually orders a lot of dishes, until the guests are truly unable to finish them all and food is left over.
If there are leftovers, it shows that the host is not stingy, and has wholeheartedly treated you to a meal.
Here comes the problem however: leaving that many leftovers would be a tremendous waste, so how do we solve this?
This is how the doggy bag culture was born.
Usually, at the end of the meal, the host escorts the guests to the restaurant’s exit.
During this time, staff prepare a doggy bag with the leftovers, ..
.. and after waiting for the guests to leave, the staff hand it over to the host.
This way, not only is food not wasted, but the host also does not lose face.
Because of these cultural differences, many Japanese people who come to China have trouble adapting.
For them, not leaving leftovers is considered polite, while Chinese people consider leaving leftovers a way of showing hospitality.
As a result, you may come upon the phenomenon where a Japanese person does their utmost to finish all the food on the table, ..
.. all while the Chinese person continues to order more as soon as the table starts running out of food.
